title: When Does Dynamic Preconditioning Preserve the Polyak-Ruppert CLT? A Stabilization Threshold
summary: Polyak-Ruppert averaging yields an asymptotically normal estimator with sandwich covariance $H^{-1}SH^{-1}$, the foundation of online inference. When the gradient step is preconditioned by a data-driven matrix $P_t$, we ask how fast $P_t$ must stabilize for the central limit theorem (CLT) to remain valid. We resolve this via an exact preconditioner-isolating decomposition of the averaged error that confines $P_t$ to a dynamic remainder $R_n$, leaving the martingale and Taylor terms preconditioner-free.
